newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares close lower in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares close lower in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower for the fifth consecutive session on Sunday in extremely low volume, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.24 percent, or 3.06 points, to 243.58 on low all-share turnover of 70 million shekels against 108 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.16 percent lower at 250.31.

"We were expecting a sharper decline considering the fact that the February CPI was relatively high. The figure was within expectations but it is still dissappointing. The Bank of Israel will not lower its key interest rate now," said Michael Weiss of Evergreen Capital Markets.
The February consumer price index, released on Friday, rose 1.2 percent compared with an 0.4 percent increase in January. The CPI was at the top of economists' forecasts.
"The political uncertainty concerning the peace process also affected trading in a negative way. Activity was very low and it's difficult to say where the market is going," Weiss added.

Israeli officials said on Sunday that work on building a Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem would start on Monday despite police warnings the project threatened to spark Palestinian violence.

"The market looks very bad. The political situation affects trading and investors show little interest in the market," Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities. "The fact that activity was so low today is very worrying."

The most active share was Leumi Insurance Holdings , which fell 2.5 percent to 259 agorot on volume of 4.5 million shekels. Assicurazioni Generali SPA on Thursday set its $308 million tender offering for shares in Leumi Insurance for this week.
Generali said it would offer 3.2755 shekels a share for up to 42.2 percent of any one shareholder's total holding.

Other active shares included Koor Industries, which fell 1.0 percent to 30,347 agorot on volume of 2.9 million shekels, and Bank Hapoalim, which lost 1.75 percent to 611 agorot on turnover of 2.8 million shekels.
